tldr: Arena is the first general evaluation platform for multi-agent intelligence, providing 35 diverse games, a building toolkit for custom multi-agent scenarios via GUI-configurable social trees and five basic multi-agent reward schemes (BMaRSs), Python implementations of five deep MARL baselines, and 100 benchmark agents/teams for stable population-level evaluation.
contributions: A general evaluation platform for multi-agent intelligence with 35 diverse games (27 new to the community, 8 inspired by existing work, and a StarCraft interface)
A building toolkit enabling easy creation of novel multi-agent scenarios through a GUI-configurable social tree and five BMaRSs
Python implementations of five state-of-the-art deep multi-agent reinforcement learning baselines for both competitive and collaborative settings
A release of 100 best agents/teams trained with different schemes per game as a base population for stable, uniform evaluation
methods: The authors built Arena on the Unity game engine, leveraging its realistic rendering, physics, visual editor, and large asset community. They designed a GUI-configurable social tree that defines agent groupings and applies one of five basic multi-agent reward schemes (BMaRSs) at each node: Non-learnable (F_NL), Isolated (F_IS), Competitive (F_CP), Collaborative (F_CL), and Competitive-Collaborative Mixed (F_CC). Each BMaRS constrains the joint reward function to produce a specific social paradigm. The platform includes 35 multi-agent games, Python implementations of baselines including decentralized PPO and self-play methods, and a population evaluation metric that ranks agents against a base population of 100 released agents/teams.
results: Arena contains 35 multi-agent games with diverse logics and representations. The platform provides 5 BMaRSs with ready-to-use reward functions and a verification option for custom reward functions. Five state-of-the-art deep MARL baselines were implemented in Python. A set of 100 best agents/teams was released as the base population for evaluation. Experiments validated the game set (stochasticity, rendering, simulation speed) and the extensible building toolkit, though detailed experimental numbers are truncated in the provided text.
limitations: The platform is built on Unity, which, while offering realistic rendering and physics, may introduce sim-to-real gaps. Many of the 35 games remain unsolved challenges for state-of-the-art algorithms. Multi-agent intelligence research is still in an early stage with many unexplored problems.
